characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy controls the scope and credibility of demonstrators proving platform-neutral Danish digital identity is architecturally viable. It maps MitID dependencies, develops non-production proof-of-concept authenticators using open standards (FIDO2/WebAuthn, OpenID Connect), and tests fallback paths on privacy-respecting platforms like GrapheneOS. Success metrics include two working demonstrators, published technical validation, and credible evidence that secure, platform-independent access is feasible without exclusive reliance on Apple or Google trust anchors.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy directly amplifies Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy by providing concrete technical evidence that platform-neutral requirements are implementable rather than theoretical. Working demonstrators reduce perceived risk for policymakers and procurement officers, making their advocacy efforts substantially more persuasive and grounded in demonstrated feasibility rather than aspiration alone.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict arises with EU Standards Engagement Strategy regarding resource allocation and timeline priorities. Deep technical work on Danish-specific demonstrators may delay or reduce capacity for contributing to broader EU standards discussions. Additionally, overly ambitious demonstrator scope risks exceeding phase-two budgets, constraining resources available for policy and coalition work that drives actual adoption leverage.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy reframes digital identity dependency as a resilience, continuity, and supplier-concentration risk rather than solely a privacy issue. It targets Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, AltID stakeholders, and relevant parliamentary bodies with formal proposals for platform-neutral access requirements and certified fallback paths. Success metrics include published policy proposals, formal written responses from authorities, and inclusion of platform-neutrality language in official AltID design or procurement documents.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy powerfully synergizes with Coalition Building Strategy and Technical Feasibility Strategy. A broad coalition amplifies advocacy reach and credibility, while working demonstrators provide evidence that neutrality requirements are technically sound. Together, these create political momentum that makes procurement language inclusion substantially more likely than advocacy alone could achieve.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict exists with EU Standards Engagement Strategy over advocacy focus and messaging. Intensive Danish procurement-level advocacy may consume capacity for EU-level standards engagement. Additionally, framing digital identity primarily through national resilience arguments may undermine EU-level arguments for harmonized, platform-neutral standards across member states.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy mobilizes stakeholders across civil society, academia, privacy advocates, security experts, contingency planners, and sympathetic parliamentary members to amplify pressure for platform neutrality. It identifies blockers, decision gates, and lead times for institutional change. Success metrics include documented stakeholder engagement, coalition diversity spanning technical and policy domains, and demonstrated political pressure reflected in official responses and procurement language.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Coalition Building Strategy creates powerful synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy. A broad, credible coalition dramatically increases the political cost of ignoring platform-neutrality proposals and strengthens negotiating leverage in procurement discussions. Civil-society and academic involvement adds legitimacy that a narrow technical effort could never achieve.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict arises with Technical Feasibility Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy regarding resource prioritization and scope creep. Building and maintaining a broad coalition requires sustained engagement effort that competes with technical development timelines. Additionally, coalition members may have conflicting priorities—academic researchers prioritizing publication versus practitioners focused on near-term procurement outcomes—creating coordination costs that can dilute focus.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy directly targets AltID procurement documents and related digital identity initiatives, seeking to embed requirements for platform-neutral access paths and fallback authentication mechanisms that reduce lock-in to Apple/Google ecosystems. It uses feasibility reports, demonstrators, and coalition support to create procurement language and standards pressure that make supplier-neutral design harder to exclude. Success metrics include specific language in official procurement documents, documented vendor responses, and demonstrable shifts in digital identity architecture decisions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Procurement Influence Strategy shows strong synergy with Technical Feasibility Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy. Working demonstrators prove requirements are implementable; credible policy proposals establish the case for change. Together, these provide procurement officers with technical evidence and political cover to include neutrality requirements without appearing unrealistic or ideologically driven.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Tension exists with EU Standards Engagement Strategy regarding jurisdiction and timing. Intensive focus on Danish AltID procurement may reduce capacity for contributing to EU-wide standards harmonization. Additionally, procurement-driven platform-neutrality requirements that diverge from emerging EU Digital Identity Wallet standards could create fragmentation rather than alignment.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy positions Danish work within European Digital Identity Wallet, eIDAS2, and related technical working groups to influence broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and platform lock-in reduction. It leverages feasibility work and demonstrators to advocate for certified fallback mechanisms and platform-neutral access at the EU level. Success metrics include documented input to relevant EU bodies, alignment language in European Digital Identity Wallet materials, and cross-member-state awareness of platform-neutrality arguments.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy synergizes with Technical Feasibility Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy by amplifying Danish work into European precedent-setting. EU-level standards adoption of platform-neutrality principles creates regulatory pressure that reinforces Danish procurement efforts and provides international legitimacy for technical choices made in demonstrators.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict arises with Procurement Influence Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy over resource allocation and timeline alignment. EU standards work operates on slower, consensus-driven timelines that may not align with urgent Danish AltID procurement windows. Additionally, broad EU engagement may dilute focus from immediate Danish institutional targets, and European consensus-building may water down specific platform-neutrality language to achieve broader political acceptability.
